metadata.title: Blue-green deployment for the orders service

content.label: How blue-green works
content.takeaway: Deploy to the idle twin, then move traffic over at once, and back the same way if needed.

content.markdown: Blue and green are identical production environments. One serves all live traffic while the other sits idle; you deploy to the idle one, test it, then move traffic in one step. Because the old one keeps running, going back is the same one-step switch. The cost: twice the infrastructure during a release.

content.label: Before you start: prerequisites
content.takeaway: All five must hold first; backward-compatible migrations are a hard requirement.

content.markdown: `orders-blue` and `orders-green`, with the same instance count, instance size and configuration.

nodes.title: A health endpoint that checks dependencies

content.markdown: `GET /healthz` returns `200` only when the service can reach its database and its queue.

The old version must keep working against the new schema. Hard requirement: both versions share one database, and a rollback does not undo a migration.

**If a migration is not backward compatible, do not use this procedure:** split it into an additive release first and a cleanup release later.

nodes.title: Access to the load balancer's listener rules

content.markdown: The service runs behind a load balancer; the switch changes which target group its listener forwards to.
A dashboard or query showing the 5xx error rate per environment, so green's errors can be told from blue's.

content.label: Release steps
content.takeaway: Blue is live: deploy and verify green, switch, watch for 15 minutes, keep blue for 24 hours.

content.label: 1. Deploy 2.8.0 to orders-green
details: Use the build artifact that passed staging
Expected: all green instances report 2.8.0; blue still serves 100% of traffic

content.label: 2. Run the database migrations once
details: From a single job, not from every instance
Expected: the job exits with code 0; blue keeps serving without new errors

content.label: 3. All green instances return 200 within 10 minutes?
4. Smoke tests pass on green?
details: Run the suite against green's internal address

content.label: 5. Switch traffic to green
details: Point the listener at the green target group
Expected: within about 30 seconds new requests go to green; blue gets no new connections

content.label: 6. 5xx error rate above 2% within 15 minutes?
details: Watch green from the moment of the switch

content.label: 7. Keep blue on standby for 24 hours
details: It is the rollback target until then
Do not run the next release's migrations while blue is on standby, or rolling back stops being safe

content.label: 8. Retire blue: scale it down
details: After 24 hours with no rollback; blue becomes the idle environment for the next release

content.label: When things go wrong: rolling back
content.takeaway: Going back is fast; the database stays as migrated.

nodes.title: Before the switch: tear down green

content.markdown: If green fails its health checks or tests, stop, tear down green and leave blue serving traffic. Nothing was switched, so customers are unaffected: this rollback is cheap.

nodes.title: After the switch: switch back to blue

content.markdown:
Run the same command with `$BLUE_TG_ARN`; all traffic returns to blue within about 30 seconds.

**Caveat:** requests in flight on green during the switch may fail and need a client retry.
